target_customer: Small and medium businesses buying cyber insurance, later managed service providers (MSPs) selling security assessments
problem: SMBs struggle to understand their cyber risk and to get suitable cyber insurance coverage and quotes.
business_model: Insurance brokerage commission plus SaaS risk assessment subscription (later sold to MSPs)
product_category: Cyber risk assessment and insurance brokerage

founders.name: Naren Sathiya
founders.background_notes: Early engineer at Hippo who led its embedded distribution channel with homebuilders, which grew to over 20% of revenue in 1.5 years (per YC page). Joined Cytracom after the sale.

technical_complexity.rationale: Outside in scanning plus a scoring model and a quote brokering workflow was feasible for a small team; most of the difficulty was insurance licensing and carrier relationships.

defensibility.rationale: Insurers such as Coalition and Cowbell ran their own scans and sold direct, so the assessment was easy to match.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Digital cyber insurers kept growing and bundled scanning with policies; Telivy shifted toward MSP customers and was acquired by Cytracom in January 2025.

market_need_then: Cyber insurance demand and premiums were rising in 2021 as ransomware spread, and At-Bay raised a reported 185M Series D at a 1.35B valuation in 2021 (from a 2026 comparison article).

branding.domain_note: telivy.com now redirects (301) to a Cytracom vulnerability management page.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand press found; the domain now redirects to the acquirer.

pivots.to: Risk assessment platform sold to MSPs
pivots.why: One profile says the main customer shifted to MSPs around 2022; the reason is not stated.

outcome_analysis: Telivy began as a cyber insurance broker for SMBs with an ML risk assessment, shifted toward selling its assessment to MSPs, and was acquired by Cytracom in January 2025 for undisclosed terms. Total funding appears to be about 2.5M from aggregator estimates, so it exited as a small company after leaning on the product rather than insurance brokerage.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights and VCBacked estimate 2.5M to 2.63M over several rounds with Thomvest, Global Founders Capital and Maschmeyer Group Ventures named by one aggregator; no press release or filing found, so no rounds recorded. One archive lists extra co-founders, which the YC page does not. HQ varies (San Francisco, Santa Cruz). Competitor list left empty: only 2026 comparison pages were found; the At-Bay 2021 raise is mentioned in market_need_then only. Pivot date approximate and single source. Completeness pass: one seed round recorded (November 2021, amount not given for the round) resting on a single database (VCBacked); totals of 2.5M to 3M USD across sources are not allocated to rounds, so the history is partial. Maschmeyer Group Ventures is named by another aggregator only. Extra co-founders (Ben Grosser, Venkata Vijay Ventrapragada) appear in an archive profile only and are not added.
